content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text rules on a link collision (D5 vs C5) after a multi-row answer, so K-C governs whether it used chain-versus-chain footing rather than a stating-verse test.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"The phrase 'leaving the sign's sense open' can be read as a substantive chain-level finding that support does not determine the sign (allowed) or as a forbidden demand for word-for-word stating; the judge wrote no contrary-verse requirement.","why":"The judge calls D5 vs C5 underdetermined because the sign's sense remains open after CR2 G answers the rows, not because no individual pressing verse states the contrary in its own words."}
